identity: 1965 Porsche 911 Type 901/01 air-cooled flat-six. Engine-mounted systems; vehicle ancillaries explicitly excluded.
objective: Explain the complete engine-mounted power, breathing, timing, cooling and lubrication architecture in a continuous 3D tour, then reassemble.

components.name: Belt & pulleys
components.purpose: The crankshaft turns a belt. That belt drives the cooling fan and alternator, so the running engine provides its own airflow.

components.name: Cooling fan
components.purpose: The pitched blades accelerate air into the shroud. Cooling needs directed flow across the hot surfaces, not simply an exposed engine.

components.name: Fan housing
components.purpose: The housing supports the fan and alternator while keeping the blade tips close to the surrounding ring. It forms the inlet to the cooling duct.

components.name: Alternator
components.purpose: Behind the fan, an alternator converts shaft rotation into electrical power. It shares the belt drive rather than needing a second motor.

components.name: Cooling shroud
components.purpose: The black shroud guides fan air over both cylinder banks. Without that guidance, air could escape before collecting heat from the fins.

components.name: Air cleaner
components.purpose: The air cleaner feeds the two banks of carburetors. Removing it reveals six separate intake throats beneath.

components.name: Solex carburetors
components.purpose: The early 901/01 uses Solex carburetion. Air passes through a throat for each cylinder; throttle position changes the flow and the carburetor meters fuel into it.

components.name: Intake manifolds
components.purpose: The intake runners connect the carburetors to the cylinder heads. An intake valve admits the mixture into the chamber at the appropriate part of the cycle.

components.name: Left cylinder heads
components.purpose: Each cylinder has its own head. The chamber closes the cylinder while the intake and exhaust valves control what enters and leaves.

components.name: Right cylinder heads
components.purpose: The opposite three cylinders work through the same four-stroke sequence. Their horizontal arrangement gives the flat-six its broad, low form.

components.name: Left cylinder bank
components.purpose: The bore guides the piston. Outside, thin fins increase the surface exposed to cooling air; the hot cylinder can shed heat as the fan drives air past.

components.name: Right cylinder bank
components.purpose: Three cylinders sit on each side of the crankcase. Opposed pistons move toward and away from the centre as their rods follow separate crankpins.

components.name: Six pistons
components.purpose: Combustion pressure pushes on each piston crown. Rings seal against the bore while the hollow skirt and wrist pin connect that force to a rod.

components.name: Connecting rods
components.purpose: Each rod connects a piston pin to its own crankpin. The big end follows a circle while the small end follows the piston, converting reciprocation into rotation.

components.name: Crankshaft
components.purpose: Six offset crankpins gather the piston forces into one rotating shaft. Main journals support it inside the case; counterweights help manage the rotating loads.

components.name: Flywheel
components.purpose: The flywheel stores rotational energy between firing impulses and passes torque toward the clutch. Its toothed perimeter also gives the starter a place to engage.

components.name: Timing covers
components.purpose: The front covers enclose the timing drive and retain lubricant. Moving them away reveals the chain route between the central drive and the two camshafts.

components.name: Timing chains
components.purpose: An intermediate drive turns two chains, one for each camshaft. Valve timing coordinates intake and exhaust events with piston travel through the four-stroke cycle.

components.name: Valve covers
components.purpose: The ribbed covers seal the valve mechanism. Removing them opens a service view of the rocker and cam assemblies beneath.

components.name: Cam carriers
components.purpose: The carriers support the camshafts and rocker shafts along each bank. Alignment matters: a cam profile is useful only if the moving surfaces meet in the right place.

components.name: Camshafts
components.purpose: One overhead camshaft serves each bank. Its lobes act through rockers to open valves; spring force closes them after the lobe passes.

components.name: Valves & rockers
components.purpose: The intake valve admits fresh mixture; the exhaust valve lets spent gases leave. Rockers transmit cam motion, and springs keep the valves returning to their seats.

components.name: Ignition system
components.purpose: The distributor routes high voltage to six spark plugs. A spark starts combustion in the compressed mixture; the plug is a separate part of each head.

components.name: Left crankcase
components.purpose: One half of the split crankcase supports the cylinders and the rotating shaft. The mating surfaces locate the other half and form the enclosed lower engine.

components.name: Right crankcase
components.purpose: The matching case half completes the main bearing supports. Bolting the halves together fixes the relationship between the crankshaft and both cylinder banks.

components.name: Oil pump
components.purpose: The dry-sump system uses pumping stages to supply pressurized oil and scavenge it back toward a separate reservoir. Oil both lubricates moving interfaces and carries heat away.

components.name: Oil cooler
components.purpose: Oil carries heat from loaded surfaces to the cooler. Closely spaced fins give the air another route to remove that heat.

components.name: Oil return & lines
components.purpose: Return tubes carry oil from the heads back toward the case. External connections link the engine to the wider dry-sump circuit in the car.

components.name: Exhaust system
components.purpose: Exhaust leaves each head through a runner, collects below the banks, and passes through the silencer. The cycle can then begin again with fresh mixture.
